title: Breaking the Top-$K$ Barrier: Advancing Top-$K$ Ranking Metrics Optimization in Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Optimizing NDCG@K during recommendation-model training is difficult because of discontinuity and Top-K truncation.

gap.claim: Existing approaches either overlook Top-K truncation or incur high computational costs and training instability.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes SoftmaxLoss@K, a recommendation loss for NDCG@K optimization.
The method uses a quantile technique for Top-K truncation and a smooth upper bound to address discontinuity.
The proposed loss is described as having theoretical guarantees, computational efficiency, gradient stability, and noise robustness.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe SoftmaxLoss@K as a novel recommendation loss.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on four real-world datasets and three recommendation backbones show a 6.03% average improvement over existing losses.
The authors report that the code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Top-K ranking metrics such as NDCG@K are presented as standard evaluation metrics for recommender systems.
Training-time optimization of NDCG@K is challenged by discontinuity and Top-K truncation.
Prior optimization efforts are characterized as incomplete, computationally expensive, or unstable.
The paper introduces SL@K, combining quantile handling of truncation with a smooth upper bound.
The authors report favorable properties and improved experimental performance, with code availability.

source_observation.claim: The method combines a quantile technique for Top-K truncation with a smooth upper bound for discontinuity.

interpretation.claim: Effective optimization of truncated ranking metrics may require addressing both truncation and discontinuity in the objective.

application.claim: When designing ranking losses, explicitly model truncation and use a differentiable surrogate for discontinuous metrics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design generalizes beyond NDCG@K.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, three backbones, baselines, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not provide the theoretical guarantees or derivations.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported improvement.
